page.layout: One page of text in a single column; margin notes in the right margin (Greek catchwords and section numbers II., III., IIII. with Greek and Latin terms). Running head at top; page number at top right.

main_text.p: Θυμίαματα non reddunt suffitum nisi succensa: habent enim humorem in se cremabilem, sed ita cum siccis & terreis partibus continuum, ut non accenda-tur humor separatim, & sine siccis terre-isq; partibus exhalare nequeant: & tota fere consumuntur ab igne.II. Καπνος.

Secundum Aristoteli dicitur καπνὸς, qui est halitus ab igne de ligno expressus: hic tamen non habet θυμιαματικὴν, licet sit inflammabilis. Corpus ligneum habet plus terrae, quam aquae. Hic halitus vulgo dicitur fumus, qui tamen non est omnis φλογιστὸς, id est, inflammabilis, sed ille qui moderate siccus & humidus, & quidem humore aereo superante.

p.i: Lignum putridum non facile ardet propter nimiam siccitatem; Spongia propter raritatem; Hebenum propter densitatem.

main_text.p: Tertium dicitur λιγνὺς, qui est halitus suffitus opimi, alias fuligo, ex pinguire, qualis est Cera, Pix, Gummi, Resina, expressus.III. Λιγνὺς.
Quartum genus est Nidor, ex iis rebus, quae pinguedinem habent madidam & evidentem, eductus, ut est oleum,IIII. Nidor.

page.notes: Marginal Greek terms are partly uncertain. Several Greek words in the text (θυμίαματα, καπνὸς, θυμιαματικὴν, φλογιστὸς, λιγνὺς) are read from a small, faded scan and may contain errors. Text near the right edge of the column is slightly obscured by show-through from the reverse page and has been read as best as possible. The catchword "leum," is printed at the foot of the column and continues on the next page as "oleum"; the final word has been split accordingly.
